41177470.clinical_problem: etiology classification (congenital heart disease, very preterm birth, spina bifida) from neonatal brain connectome
41177470.patient_population: 51 newborns with congenital heart disease, 100 born very preterm, and 43 with spina bifida aperta (194 neonates total)
41177470.model_description: Input is structural brain connectomes derived from MRI, parcellated at the voxel level rather than with a predefined atlas. A graph convolutional network is trained to classify neonates by etiology (congenital heart disease, very preterm birth, or spina bifida aperta), outperforming atlas-based and multilayer-perceptron baselines (F1 0.78 vs 0.62 and 0.69). It is presented as a research method for studying etiology-specific connectome patterns, not a clinical tool.
41177470.dataset_size: 194 neonates (51 CHD, 100 very preterm, 43 spina bifida aperta)
41177470.headline_result: F1 = 0.78 (voxel-level GNN) vs 0.62 (atlas-based) vs 0.69 (multilayer-perceptron baseline) for etiology classification

41272514.clinical_problem: ADHD classification from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity
41272514.patient_population: children with ADHD (n=40) and healthy control children (n=45); exact age range not stated
41272514.model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional connectivity split into three low-frequency sub-bands (Slow3, Slow4, Slow5). A machine-learning classifier of unspecified type uses connectivity features from each sub-band to separate children with ADHD from healthy controls. Classification accuracy ranged from 79-85% depending on the frequency band, proposed as a candidate biomarker rather than a diagnostic tool.
41272514.headline_result: Accuracy 79% (ADHD) / 82% (HC) in the Slow3 band and 85%/80% in the combined Slow4/Slow5 band; AUC 0.755 and 0.783 respectively

41292958.model_family: connectome-based predictive modeling (cross-validated, data-driven machine learning)
41292958.clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive performance from functional connectivity associated with environmental exposome
41292958.patient_population: early adolescents enrolled in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study; exact ages not given
41292958.model_description: Input is resting-state and task fMRI functional connectivity from adolescents in the ABCD Study. A cross-validated, data-driven connectome-based predictive model relates connectivity patterns to an environmental 'exposome' score and to cognitive performance across three domains (general cognition, executive function, learning/memory). Results generalized across data-collection sites and cognitive domains, but this is a research association study, not a diagnostic tool.
41292958.dataset_size: n = 6,137-8,391 across models, ABCD Study cohort
41292958.headline_result: Cross-validated models: r = 0.34-0.44, p < .001, robust across data-collection sites and cognitive domains (p < 0.0009)

41407149.clinical_problem: classifying resilience vs susceptibility to childhood adversity from fear-learning brain network connectivity
41407149.patient_population: 213 participants with fear-learning fMRI data; abstract does not give an exact age range but indexing terms include adolescents alongside young adults and adults
41407149.model_description: Input is task-based fMRI functional connectivity acquired during a fear-learning paradigm, summarized as whole-brain network graph-theory metrics. A network-connectivity-based model classifies participants as resilient or susceptible to childhood unpredictability, using psychological (depressive symptoms) and biological (TNF-alpha) resilience markers, with 89% classification accuracy. It is presented as a research tool for studying neural correlates of resilience, not a clinical predictor.
41407149.headline_result: Network connectivity-based models classified resilient vs susceptible groups with 89% accuracy

41541224.model_family: linear regression models and random forest
41541224.clinical_problem: predicting adolescent rumination (a depression risk marker) from dynamic resting-state fMRI connectivity
41541224.patient_population: 443 adolescents, including clinical and non-clinical individuals (largest sample to date for this analysis)
41541224.model_description: Input is dynamic (time-varying) resting-state fMRI connectivity from a large adolescent sample. Linear models (including one previously validated in adults) and an exploratory random forest were trained to predict self-reported rumination from default-mode-network and whole-brain dynamic connectivity features. None of the models generalized to an external held-out sample with different rumination levels and scanner protocol, though the random forest showed a nominal association in the training sample.
41541224.headline_result: Adult-trained and adolescent-trained connectivity models failed to generalize to an external sample; exploratory random forest showed only a nominal association with rumination in training data
41541224.study_design: cross-sectional predictive modeling with external generalization test

41618988.model_family: support vector machine (SVM) with leave-one-out cross-validation
41618988.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric bipolar disorder (with or without psychotic symptoms) from healthy controls using diffusion tensor imaging white matter metrics
41618988.patient_population: 27 patients with pediatric bipolar disorder and psychotic symptoms, 25 with pediatric bipolar disorder without psychosis, and 19 healthy controls
41618988.model_description: Input is diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics (fractional, mean, radial and axial diffusivity) from standard, free-water-corrected, and superficial white matter models. A support vector machine with leave-one-out cross-validation uses regional DTI metrics to distinguish children/adolescents with pediatric bipolar disorder (with or without psychotic symptoms) from healthy controls. The abstract states the altered regions could effectively discriminate the groups but gives no numeric accuracy.
41618988.dataset_size: 71 participants (27 PBD with psychosis, 25 PBD without psychosis, 19 healthy controls)
41618988.headline_result: SVM analyses with leave-one-out cross-validation reportedly discriminated PBD patients from healthy controls using altered DTI metrics; no accuracy percentage given

41727084.clinical_problem: predicting lapses in interoceptive attention from fMRI brain connectivity and breathing signals in adolescents with depressive symptoms
41727084.model_description: Input is task fMRI (breath-counting task) connectivity plus simultaneous breathing and button-press behavioral data from adolescents with depressive symptoms. Machine-learning models of unspecified type, trained on a split training/validation sample, predict moments of 'interoceptive attention lapse' from behavioral timing, breathing variability, and whole-brain connectivity (default-mode, attention, and somatomotor networks). Whole-brain connectivity models modestly improved prediction over behavior alone.
41727084.headline_result: AUC > 0.75 for behavioral predictors; AUC ≈ 0.65 for whole-brain connectivity model predicting attention lapses

41881121.clinical_problem: distinguishing adolescent major depressive disorder from bipolar disorder using resting-state fMRI network features
41881121.patient_population: 125 adolescents aged 12-19 years (48 with major depressive disorder, 36 with bipolar disorder, 41 healthy controls)
41881121.model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional network features, including nodal centrality and clustering coefficient from graph-theoretical analysis. A support vector machine trained on these network features distinguishes adolescent major depressive disorder from bipolar disorder, driven mainly by insula and cingulate gyrus features. It is presented as a research classifier, not a validated diagnostic test.
41881121.dataset_size: 125 adolescents (48 MDD, 36 bipolar disorder, 41 healthy controls)
41881121.headline_result: SVM classifier distinguished adolescent MDD from bipolar disorder with 88.24% accuracy (p < 0.001)

42129352.clinical_problem: predicting 1-year eating-behavior outcomes in children with obesity from reward/inhibitory-control brain connectivity
42129352.patient_population: 38 children with overweight/obesity and 68 normal-weight children; exact age range not stated
42129352.model_description: Input is resting-state functional connectivity and dynamic-causal-modeling-derived effective connectivity between prefrontal cortex and caudate, in children with and without overweight/obesity. A machine-learning approach uses baseline connectivity between these regions to predict changes in eating behavior one year later. The abstract reports that baseline caudate-prefrontal connections were predictive of behavior change but gives no numeric accuracy.
42129352.headline_result: Baseline caudate-prefrontal connectivity predicted 1-year change in children's eating behavior; no accuracy metric reported

42183358.clinical_problem: brain-age prediction from longitudinal resting-state fMRI to flag neurodevelopmental risk
42183358.patient_population: 633 children followed longitudinally from birth to age 10 years (1,436 resting-state fMRI scans total)
42183358.model_description: Input is longitudinal resting-state fMRI (1,436 scans from 633 children followed from birth to age 10) used to build normative functional-connectivity growth curves. A deep-learning brain-age prediction model is trained on this data and flags disorder-specific deviations that distinguish neurodevelopmental risk groups in early childhood; early connectivity measures also predicted socioemotional and cognitive outcomes at ages 8 and 10. No accuracy metric for the brain-age model is given in the abstract.
42183358.dataset_size: 1,436 resting-state fMRI scans from 633 children, birth to age 10
42183358.headline_result: Deep-learning brain-age model distinguished neurodevelopmental risk groups; early connectivity predicted 8- and 10-year socioemotional/cognitive outcomes (no accuracy figure given)

42265860.clinical_problem: distinguishing children with developmental dyslexia from typical readers using fMRI connectome-based classification
42265860.patient_population: children with Developmental Dyslexia and Typical Readers; sample size not stated
42265860.model_description: Input is task and 'pseudo-resting' fMRI connectomes derived by regressing task-related activity out of visual-task fMRI data. A support vector machine trained on these connectomes discriminates children with developmental dyslexia from typical readers in both task and pseudo-resting conditions. This is primarily a methods investigation of preprocessing choices rather than a clinical diagnostic tool, and no accuracy figure is reported.
42265860.headline_result: SVM effectively discriminated developmental dyslexia from typical readers in task and pseudo-resting fMRI conditions; no accuracy percentage reported
42265860.study_design: methods/technical study (task-fMRI preprocessing) with case-control classification

42332286.clinical_problem: predicting lapses in interoceptive attention from fMRI brain connectivity and breathing signals in adolescents with anxiety/depressive symptoms
42332286.patient_population: 93 adolescents enriched for generalized anxiety disorder and depression symptoms
42332286.model_description: Input is task fMRI (breath-counting task) connectivity plus simultaneous breathing and button-press behavioral data from adolescents enriched for anxiety and depression symptoms. Machine-learning models of unspecified type, trained and tested on split training/validation sets, predict moments of 'interoceptive attention lapse' from behavioral timing, breathing variability, and whole-brain connectivity (default-mode, attention, and somatomotor networks). Whole-brain connectivity models modestly improved prediction over behavior alone.
42332286.headline_result: AUC > 0.75 for behavioral predictors; AUC ≈ 0.65 for whole-brain connectivity model predicting attention lapses

42482506.body_region: brain (fronto-limbic network: insula, anterior cingulate, orbitofrontal cortex, hippocampus)
42482506.clinical_problem: predicting non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents with major depressive disorder from dynamic functional connectivity
42482506.patient_population: 204 adolescents with major depressive disorder (154 with non-suicidal self-injury, 50 without)
42482506.model_description: Input is dynamic (time-varying) resting-state fMRI connectivity within the fronto-limbic network. A machine-learning model trained on these dynamic connectivity features predicts non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) status in adolescents with major depressive disorder, and mediation analysis links reduced connectivity variability to the depression-NSSI relationship. It is presented as a research finding on candidate neural markers, not a clinical test.
42482506.headline_result: Machine-learning model predicted NSSI status with mean AUC 0.84 (PR-AUC 0.94)

42501730.clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive performance from functional connectivity associated with environmental exposome
